content.text:
I fixed the bug: two `OrderedSet`s with the same elements now give the same `hashCode()`. All 44 existing test suites pass. I didn't add a regression test, so the hidden tests will be the real check.

**Cause:** when you remove an item from an `OrderedMap` (which `OrderedSet` is built on), it leaves an empty slot in its internal list instead of shifting everything down. `OrderedMap.__iterate` in `src/OrderedMap.js` skipped those empty slots when calling back, but the count it returned still included them. `hashCollection` mixes that count into the hash. So a set you got to by removing elements hashed differently from a freshly built set with the same contents.

**Fix:** `__iterate` now counts only real entries. If the callback stops the loop early, the entry it stopped on is still counted, which matches how the other collections count.

**Check:** I built a 100-element `OrderedSet` and trimmed it down to `90..99` four ways: one-by-one `remove`, `withMutations`, `subtract`, and `filter`. Before the fix, the first three gave hash `-499679352` while a fresh `OrderedSet(Range(90, 100))` gave `71407705`. After the fix, all four give `71407705`.
